_comment: Annual events whose own site states the date only in a sentence, read by mapsee_ingest_annual.py. Identity, venue and coordinates are curated here; the DATE, the clock and the publisher's own FREE sentence are read from the site on every run and never stored, as fair_sources.json does. shape 'day': the site is the event's own, single days count, and name_rx is required and names the EVENT, not the organiser ('short\s+run\s+comix', not 'short\s+run': every post on an organiser's homepage says its name, and the nearest named date wins); a date is believed only with that name within 90 characters before it, never across another date, or in its own paragraph. shape 'range': ranges only, as the fairs adapter. 'months' (optional) is the event's own months, curated from its past editions: a date whose start month is outside it is never the event, whatever words surround it; '_months' says where the months came from. 'pages' (optional) are read in order only while the homepage has given nothing upcoming and has not said the edition's own hours ended today; no other link is followed. The venue is re-checked against the publisher each edition: it is curated, not scraped.

sites.name: Short Run Comix Festival
sites._months: Five editions on the saved homepage (read 2026-11-07), each a Saturday in Nov 1-7, the first Saturday of November: 2026-11-07 (the hero), 2025-11-01 ('Saturday, Nov. 1st', post of 2025-09-20), 2024-11-02 ('Nov. 2nd', post of 2024-08-27), 2023-11-04 ('Nov. 4th', post of 2023-09-11) and 2022-11-05 ('Nov. 5th', post of 2022-09-14). No edition in any other month. October is margin for a move a week earlier, not evidence. A date outside these months is never the festival, whatever words surround it (exhibitor applications, anthology submissions, a Spring Market).
